text.p: Here are highlights of stories in the Romanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The government will cut subsidises to animal farms, the paper says.
- Foreign investments in Romania amounted to $2.22 billion in February.
- One in two commercial companies breached laws in 1996, Financial police investigations showed.
- Costs related to the planned restructuring of Romania's steel sector could amount to $2.6 billion.
- First batch of 500 Cielo cars made by the Craiova-based Automobile Craiova SA car maker will be exported to Russia on Wednesday.
- Trade unions plan series of strikes to protest against what they called failure of the government to present clear restructuring programmes for various industrial sectors.
- Miners' trade union in the Jiu Valley coalfield refused to sign agreement between government and other trade unions to work together on the restructuring project in the mining sector.
- Offers in the tender called by the National roads administration to modernise the Bucharest-Pitesti highway ranged from 239 billion to 391 billion lei.
- An earthquake measuring 5.0 degrees on the Richter scale shook Romania on Saturday but there were no reports of damage.
- Prices for energy, natural gas and urban transport went up starting March 1, the paper says.
- The restructuring of refineries in the Ploiesti oilfield will seriously affect the population living in the area, the paper says.
- The Sidex SA steel plant in Galati stopped deliveries of steel products to its bad debtors, the paper says.
